_what: The words and shape of the graph document patch (graph-patch.mjs): a patch evolves a stored graph document by typed operations. `scopes` name each kind of thing a document holds, where it lives and which fields name it; `ops` are the operations, each a row of an action on a scope with the fields it takes (required or optional). Which fields a scope may have set comes from graph-contract.json's allowed_fields, never from here. `referenced_by` names the places that point at a thing, so removing it removes what pointed at it. `corrections` is the overlay of human fixes kept beside an inferred document: a row selects nodes by id or a glob (`*` matches any run of characters) and says what to exclude, rename, re-describe or move; the same rows apply again after every regeneration. Adding an operation is one row in `ops`; adding a place a document keeps things is one row in `scopes`.

errors.UNKNOWN_FIELD: {path} is not a field this patch takes.
errors.WRONG_TYPE: {path} has the wrong type: {expected} was expected.
errors.WRONG_GRAPH: {path} names the graph "{found}"; this document is "{expected}".
errors.STALE_BASE: {path} was written against {found}, but this document is {expected}. Read the document again and rewrite the patch.
errors.RESULT_MISMATCH: {path} says the result is {expected}, but applying the operations gives {found}.
errors.UNKNOWN_OP: {path} names the operation "{found}"; the operations are {ops}.
errors.NOT_FOUND: {path} points at {scope} "{found}", which the document does not hold.
errors.ALREADY_EXISTS: {path} adds {scope} "{found}", which the document already holds.
errors.AFTER_NOT_FOUND: {path} puts it after "{found}", which is not there.
errors.NOT_SETTABLE: {path} sets "{found}", which cannot be set on {scope}. It can set: {settable}.
errors.INVALID_RESULT: The patched document is not valid: {first}
